mainTopic: Two פסוקים about הכשר, אביי's answer that some הכשר is only מדרבנן, and the Torah source for חיבת הקודש
overview: The גמרא first asks whether one of two פסוקים about הכשר comes to exclude holy food (חיבת הקודש). It answers that one פסוק is for טומאת מת and one is for טומאת שרץ. Both are needed, because each kind of טומאה is stricter in its own way. Next, רב יוסף and רבי זירא challenge רבי אלעזר from cases where food becomes susceptible without water: a slaughtered animal, and grapes harvested for the winepress. אביי answers both: the חכמים treated these like הכשר by water, only מדרבנן. רב יוסף objects that this answer would also settle ריש לקיש's question about dry holy flour. אביי replies that ריש לקיש was asking about burning, which needs טומאה מדאורייתא. This shows that ריש לקיש holds חיבת הקודש is דאורייתא, so the גמרא searches for its source. A proof from the start of ויקרא 7:19 fails, because the animal may have been wet from a river. The end of the פסוק, which includes wood and frankincense, proves that holiness alone makes things able to become טמא.

steps.title: Maybe the extra verse excludes holy food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that one of the two פסוקים about הכשר comes to exclude food that becomes able to take on טומאה because of חיבת הקודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't the extra verse coming to exclude food that can take on impurity only because it is holy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to two פסוקים that both teach the need for הכשר. It suggests that the second one has a special job: to exclude holy food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two פסוקים teach the same thing, one looks extra. The גמרא tries to give that extra פסוק a purpose: limiting the rule so that it does not cover food that is open to טומאה only because of חיבת הקודש. This is offered as a possible proof, and the next step tests it.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it...? (opens a suggested proof)
To exclude; to leave something out of a rule
The special status of holy food, which can make it able to become טמא even without the usual liquids

phrases.english: Is it not to exclude items made susceptible through regard for sanctity?
phrases.notes: He means: holy food that can take on טומאה because it is holy, not because liquid touched it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from before this section about the two פסוקים requiring הכשר.
steps.raayaObject: That food which is susceptible only through חיבת הקודש is left out of the הכשר rule
steps.raayaSupportSource: The apparently extra second פסוק about הכשר

steps.title: No, one verse is about a corpse and one is about a creeping animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the two פסוקים are not extra, because one teaches הכשר for טומאת מת and the other for טומאת שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. One verse is about impurity from a dead person, and one verse is about impurity from a dead creeping animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from step 1. Neither verse is extra; each one covers a different source of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested proof only worked if one פסוק had nothing else to teach. By giving each פסוק its own case, טומאת מת and טומאת שרץ, the גמרא takes away the reason to read one of them as excluding holy food.

keyTerms.meaning: One (here: one of the two verses)
Impurity from a human corpse
Impurity from the carcass of one of the eight creeping animals

phrases.english: No: one is about impurity of a corpse,
and one is about impurity of a creeping animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא: חַד בְּטוּמְאַת מֵת וְחַד בְּטוּמְאַת שֶׁרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that either פסוק is extra and free to exclude חיבת הקודש
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each פסוק is needed for its own source of טומאה, so neither is free for another teaching

steps.title: Why the corpse verse alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that if the תורה had taught הכשר only for טומאת מת, we might think a שרץ, which is stricter in one way, does not need הכשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both verses are needed. If the תורה had told us only about a corpse, we would say that there food needs to be made susceptible, because a corpse does not make things impure with a lentil-sized piece. But a creeping animal does make things impure with a lentil-sized piece, so we would say food there does not need to be made susceptible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up step 2 by showing why both פסוקים are truly needed. This is the first half: why we could not learn שרץ from מת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שרץ makes things טמא with a piece as small as a lentil, which is a smaller amount than is needed for a corpse. Because שרץ is stricter in this way, we might have thought its טומאה reaches food even without הכשר. So the תורה must state the rule for שרץ on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: They are needed; both teachings are necessary
It had taught us
Making food able to take on טומאה, normally through contact with one of seven liquids
The size of a lentil, the smallest amount of a שרץ that makes things טמא
I might say; one might think

phrases.english: And they are needed, for if it had taught us impurity of a corpse,
it is there that it requires being made susceptible,
because it does not make impure with a lentil-bulk,
but a creeping animal, which makes impure with a lentil-bulk,
I would say it does not require being made susceptible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejection in step 2 by showing the שרץ verse is not extra.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing each verse teaches something we could not learn from the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since שרץ makes things טמא even with a lentil-sized piece, its טומאה might reach food without הכשר
steps.terutzMaskana: A separate פסוק is needed to teach that שרץ also requires הכשר

steps.title: Why the creeping-animal verse alone would not be enough, so both are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the other half: if the תורה had taught only שרץ, we might think מת, which makes things טמא for seven days, does not need הכשר. So both פסוקים are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had told us only about a creeping animal, we would say food needs to be made susceptible there because a creeping animal does not cause seven-day impurity. But a corpse does cause seven-day impurity, so we would say food there does not need to be made susceptible. Therefore both verses are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא. Each kind of טומאה is stricter in its own way, so neither can be learned from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מת is stricter than שרץ because it makes people and vessels טמא for seven days. With only the שרץ פסוק, we might think the stricter מת does not need הכשר. Since each one is stricter in a different way, both פסוקים are needed, and neither is free to exclude חיבת הקודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Seven-day impurity, the kind caused by a corpse
It is needed; closes a צריכותא

steps.whatToRemember: Each פסוק about הכשר has its own job, one for מת and one for שרץ, because each is stricter in a different way: lentil size for שרץ, seven days for מת. So the attempt to read one פסוק as excluding חיבת הקודש fails.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us a creeping animal,
I would say that is because it does not cause seven-day impurity,
but a corpse, which causes seven-day impurity,
I would say it does not require being made susceptible. So both are needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided צריכותא begun in step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both פסוקים are needed, one for מת and one for שרץ, so neither excludes חיבת הקודש.

steps.title: רב יוסף challenges from רבי שמעון: slaughter makes it fully susceptible
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges רבי אלעזר's view from the משנה, where רבי שמעון says the animal was made susceptible through שחיטה, even for counting ראשון and שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף raised an objection: רבי שמעון says they were made susceptible by the slaughter. They were made susceptible completely, even to count first-degree and second-degree impurity in them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge begins. רב יוסף quotes רבי שמעון from the משנה to argue against רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that levels of טומאה like ראשון and שני are counted only in food made susceptible by liquids. רבי שמעון says שחיטה alone makes the meat susceptible, and the גמרא reads this as fully susceptible, even for counting ראשון and שני. That contradicts רבי אלעזר, since there was no liquid here.

keyTerms.meaning: They were made susceptible to טומאה
Kosher slaughter
To count
First-degree and second-degree impurity, the descending levels of טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not saying the meat is already טמא. He is saying שחיטה makes it able to become טמא, the same way liquid usually does.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raises an objection:
Rabbi Shimon says: They were made susceptible by the slaughter.
They were made susceptible, even to count in them
first-degree and second-degree impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge against רבי אלעזר's rule, after the side discussion about the two פסוקים ends.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's rule that ראשון and שני are counted only in food made susceptible by liquids
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון holds that שחיטה, without any liquid, makes the meat fully susceptible, even to count ראשון and שני

steps.title: Why is the slaughtered animal susceptible without water?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף finishes his challenge: according to רבי שמעון the slaughtered animal is fully susceptible to טומאה, yet it never came into contact with water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is it susceptible? It is not food that came into contact with water!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף spells out the problem with the משנה he quoted in the last step. The animal never touched water, so how can it become fully able to take on טומאה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that food needs real contact with water (הכשר) before it can become טמא. רבי שמעון says שחיטה alone makes the animal susceptible, even for counting ראשון and שני. That seems to contradict רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Why? (used here to raise a difficulty)
Food that came into contact with water, the normal way food gets הכשר
The step that makes food able to take on טומאה

phrases.english: Why?
phrases.notes: He means: why is the slaughtered animal susceptible to טומאה in every way, as רבי שמעון said?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא לָאו אוֹכֶל הַבָּא בְּמַיִם הוּא!
phrases.english: But it is not food that came into contact with water!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? וְהָא לָאו אוֹכֶל הַבָּא בְּמַיִם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge that רב יוסף began in step 5 by stating exactly what the difficulty is.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's view that only food that came into contact with water can get הכשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון makes the animal fully susceptible through שחיטה alone, without any water.

steps.title: אביי: the חכמים treated it like water, as a rabbinic rule
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the susceptibility through שחיטה is only מדרבנן. The חכמים gave it the status of הכשר done by water.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: They treated it like הכשר by water, by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רבי אלעזר. He says the animal is not susceptible from the תורה; the חכמים made a rule that treats it as if it had touched water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the תורה, רבי אלעזר's rule still stands: without water there is no הכשר. רבי שמעון is describing a rabbinic rule. So the משנה does not contradict רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the חכמים) made it, they treated it as
By rabbinic law, not from the תורה

phrases.english: אביי said to him:
They treated it like הכשר by water, by rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: עֲשָׂאוּהוּ כְּהֶכְשֵׁר מַיִם מִדְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge from steps 5-6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the ruling from Torah law to rabbinic law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון means the animal is susceptible from the תורה without water.
steps.terutzMaskana: The susceptibility is only מדרבנן, so רבי אלעזר's Torah-level rule is untouched.

steps.title: רבי זירא's challenge from grapes harvested for the winepress
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא brings a ברייתא: grapes harvested for the winepress become susceptible, according to שמאי, and הלל was silent. But the grapes never came into contact with water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Come and hear. One who harvests grapes for the winepress: שמאי says they became susceptible, הלל says they did not, and הלל was silent before שמאי. Why? They are not food that came into contact with water!
steps.whatsHappening: A second challenge to רבי אלעזר. רבי זירא brings a case where food becomes susceptible without proper contact with water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The juice that comes out of grapes during the harvest gives them הכשר. In the end even הלל went quiet, which means he accepted שמאי's view. But this is not food that came into water the normal way, so רבי אלעזר seems to be contradicted again.

keyTerms.meaning: One who harvests grapes to bring them to the winepress
It became susceptible to טומאה
And he was silent before him (he accepted the other view)

phrases.english: רבי זירא said: Come and hear,
one who harvests grapes for the winepress –
שמאי says: they became susceptible,
הלל says: they did not become susceptible,
and הלל was silent before שמאי.
Why?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא לָאו אוֹכֶל הַבָּא בְּמַיִם הוּא!
phrases.english: But it is not food that came into contact with water!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: תָּא שְׁמַע, הַבּוֹצֵר לְגַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge against the same view of רבי אלעזר, from a different source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's view that only food that came into contact with water can get הכשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The accepted ruling makes grapes susceptible without proper contact with water.

steps.title: אביי gives the same answer: it is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers רבי זירא exactly as he answered רב יוסף: the חכמים treated the grapes as if they had received הכשר by water, by rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: They treated it like הכשר by water, by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי uses the same answer again. The grapes are susceptible only מדרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling about the grapes is a rabbinic rule, not a law from the תורה. So רבי אלעזר's principle still holds מדאורייתא.

phrases.english: אביי said to him:
They treated it like הכשר by water, by rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: עֲשָׂאוּהוּ כְּהֶכְשֵׁר מַיִם מִדְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge from step 8, using the same answer as step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the ruling from Torah law to rabbinic law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The grapes are susceptible from the תורה without water.

steps.title: רב יוסף: then ריש לקיש's question has an easy answer too
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף objects to אביי's repeated answer. If everything can be called a rabbinic הכשר, then ריש לקיש's question about dry holy flour should also be answered that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: I told you 'they became susceptible through שחיטה,' and you told me 'they treated it like הכשר by water.' רבי זירא told you his case, and you told him 'they treated it like הכשר by water.' Then for ריש לקיש too, say 'they treated it like הכשר by water'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks אביי's answer itself. If that answer works every time, ריש לקיש would have had nothing to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש asked whether dry holy flour, which is open to טומאה only because of חיבת הקודש, counts levels like ראשון and שני. If אביי's answer were right, that question would be easy: the חכמים treated it like הכשר by water, so the levels are counted מדרבנן. The fact that ריש לקיש asked at all suggests אביי's answer proves too much.

keyTerms.meaning: The special importance of holy things, which might make them susceptible to טומאה without water
Also, too

phrases.english: רב יוסף said to him:
I told you 'they became susceptible through שחיטה,'
phrases.notes: He is pointing back to his own challenge from רבי שמעון's words in the משנה (step 5).

phrases.aramaic: וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ לִי עֲשָׂאוּהוּ כְּהֶכְשֵׁר מַיִם,
phrases.english: and you told me 'they treated it like הכשר by water,'
and רבי זירא told you his case,
and you told him 'they treated it like הכשר by water,'
then for ריש לקיש too
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש asked whether dry holy flour, never mixed with oil, counts levels like ראשון and שני when it is open to טומאה only through חיבת הקודש.

phrases.english: say 'they treated it like הכשר by water'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמֵינָא לָךְ אֲנָא הוּכְשְׁרוּ בִּשְׁחִיטָה וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ לִי עֲשָׂאוּהוּ כְּהֶכְשֵׁר מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer אביי gave in steps 7 and 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's repeated answer that the הכשר is only מדרבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that answer always works, ריש לקיש's question would have had an obvious answer, so why did he need to ask it?

steps.title: ריש לקיש was asking about burning, which needs טומאה מדאורייתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that ריש לקיש was not asking about a rabbinic level where the flour is just left in doubt. He was asking whether it must be burned, which happens only with טומאה מדאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do you think ריש לקיש was asking about leaving it in doubt? He was asking about burning it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his answer. He shows that a rabbinic answer would not settle ריש לקיש's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holy food that is טמא only מדרבנן is left in doubt: it is neither eaten nor burned. It is burned only when it is טמא from the תורה. ריש לקיש wanted to know about burning, so he was asking about the דאורייתא level, and a rabbinic הכשר would not answer that.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you think? (introduces a rejected assumption)
To leave in doubt: neither eat it nor burn it
To burn it, the law for holy food that is טמא from the תורה

steps.whatToRemember: אביי keeps רבי אלעזר's view by saying that שחיטה and the grape juice give הכשר only מדרבנן. ריש לקיש's question is still a real question because it was about burning, which only follows Torah-level טומאה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think טומאה מדרבנן and טומאה מדאורייתא lead to the same result for holy food. טומאה מדרבנן means the food is left in doubt; only טומאה מדאורייתא means it must be burned.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Do you think ריש לקיש
was asking about leaving it in doubt?
When he asks, it is about burning it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ לִתְלוֹת קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's objection from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pins down what the question was really about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש's question could be answered by saying the הכשר is rabbinic.
steps.terutzMaskana: ריש לקיש was asking about burning, which requires Torah-level טומאה. So a rabbinic answer does not resolve his question.

steps.title: Where does the תורה teach that חיבת הקודש works?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that ריש לקיש treats חיבת הקודש as a rule דאורייתא, and asks for its source in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can learn from this that חיבת הקודש is from the תורה. Where do we learn that from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from ריש לקיש's question in the previous step and then asks for its source. This sets up the search that fills the rest of this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש asked whether the dry holy flour must be burned, and burning only happens with Torah-level טומאה. So he must hold that חיבת הקודש makes holy food able to become טמא on a Torah level. Now the גמרא wants to find the פסוק behind that.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference, meaning we learn it indirectly from something else that was said
The special regard for holy things, which makes holy food able to become טמא even without liquid
From the Torah, a Torah-level law
From where do we know this?

steps.confusionAlert: Normally food can only become טמא after a liquid has touched it (this is called הכשר). חיבת הקודש is the idea that holy food skips that requirement because it is so important.

phrases.english: By inference, regard for holiness is a Torah-level law;
phrases.notes: The inference comes from ריש לקיש's question about burning the dry holy flour, which we saw in the last step.

phrases.english: from where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּחִיבַּת הַקֹּדֶשׁ דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, מְנָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from אביי's explanation of ריש לקיש and opens a search for its Torah source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source showing that חיבת הקודש makes holy food able to become טמא.

steps.title: Proposed source: the פסוק about holy meat touching טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the פסוק 'והבשר אשר יגע בכל טמא' and asks what made that meat able to become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say we learn it from the פסוק 'And the meat that touches anything טמא': this meat that became able to receive טומאה, through what did that happen?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a פסוק as the source and asks a test question about it. The answer will decide whether the proof works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says holy meat becomes טמא when it touches טומאה, so the meat must have been able to receive טומאה. If no liquid could have done that, the only explanation left is חיבת הקודש. The next steps test each liquid that might have done it.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion the גמרא is about to test)
Became able to receive טומאה (received הכשר)
Through what? By what means?

phrases.english: If you say it is from what is written:
"And the meat that touches anything impure"
this meat that became able to receive impurity, through what did that happen?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a candidate פסוק in answer to the question of step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That חיבת הקודש is a Torah-level rule.

steps.title: It cannot be the animal's blood
steps.stepSummary: Blood of קדשים does not make food able to become טמא, so the blood cannot explain the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the meat became able to receive טומאה through its blood, that is hard. רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: How do we know that blood of קדשים does not do this? The פסוק says, 'Do not eat it; pour it on the ground like water.' Blood that is poured out like water does it. Blood that is not poured out like water does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possible liquid, the animal's own blood, and rejects it using a teaching of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood of ordinary animals is poured on the ground like water, so it counts as a liquid that can do הכשר. Blood of קדשים goes on the מזבח instead, so it does not do הכשר. That means it cannot be what made the holy meat in the פסוק able to become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood of sacrificial animals
Makes food able to receive טומאה
Poured out like water

phrases.english: If you say it became able to receive impurity through blood,
but didn't Rabbi Chiya bar Abba say
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
From where do we know that blood of sacrifices does not make food able to receive impurity?
As it says: "Do not eat it;
pour it on the ground like water."
Blood that is poured out like water makes food able to receive impurity;
blood that is not poured out like water does not!
phrases.notes: He means sacrificial blood, which goes on the מזבח instead of being poured on the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא דְּאִתַּכְשַׁר בְּדָם, וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first answer to the question 'במאי' from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that the meat in the פסוק became able to receive טומאה through its blood.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן learns from a פסוק that blood of קדשים does not do הכשר.

steps.title: It cannot be the liquids of the בית המקדש slaughterhouse
steps.stepSummary: The liquids of the בית המקדש slaughterhouse do not do הכשר, so they cannot explain the פסוק either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe the meat became able to receive טומאה through the liquids of the slaughterhouse. But רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: The liquids of the slaughterhouse are not only טהור, they also do not make food able to receive טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second possible liquid, the liquids in the slaughter area of the בית המקדש, and rejects it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא teaches that these liquids are special in two ways. They cannot become טמא themselves, and they also cannot give food a הכשר. So they cannot be what made the meat in the פסוק able to become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: The liquids (water and blood) of the slaughter area in the בית המקדש
Not only (literally: it is not enough that...)
Pure, טהור

phrases.english: Rather, it became able to receive impurity through the liquids of the slaughterhouse.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, say:
The liquids of the slaughterhouse:
not only are they pure,
but they also do not make food able to receive impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּאִיתַּכְשַׁר בְּמַשְׁקֵי בֵּית מַטְבְּחַיָּא, וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After blood was ruled out, tests and rejects the slaughterhouse liquids.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that slaughterhouse liquids made the meat able to receive טומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא rules that slaughterhouse liquids do not do הכשר.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's rule cannot be limited to blood
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say רבי יוסי meant only blood, but he said 'liquids', in the plural.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say we should explain his statement as being only about blood: but he said 'liquids'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks an escape route. Someone might try to save the slaughterhouse-liquids option by limiting רבי יוסי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוסי meant only blood, then the slaughterhouse water could still have given the meat its הכשר. But his wording 'משקי' is plural and covers all the liquids there, water included. So this option stays rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (bringing up a possible answer in order to reject it)
Explain it, interpret it
He is saying

phrases.english: And if you say: explain it as being about blood only,
but he said "liquids"!
phrases.notes: "Liquids" is plural, so it covers the water too, not just the blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shuts down a possible defense of the slaughterhouse-liquids option from step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The attempt to limit רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's rule to blood only.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His wording 'משקי' is plural and includes all the slaughterhouse liquids.

steps.title: So it must be חיבת הקודש
steps.stepSummary: With every liquid ruled out, the גמרא suggests the meat became able to receive טומאה through חיבת הקודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not that the meat became able to receive טומאה through חיבת הקודש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. Since no liquid could have done it, חיבת הקודש must be the reason, and that would make it a rule דאורייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works by elimination. The פסוק requires the meat to be able to become טמא, and both blood and slaughterhouse liquids are ruled out. That leaves חיבת הקודש, which shows it works on a Torah level.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not...? (the way the גמרא brings its proof to a close)

phrases.english: Rather, is it not
that it became able to receive impurity through regard for holiness?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the elimination begun in step 13 and concludes in favor of חיבת הקודש.
steps.raayaObject: That חיבת הקודש is a Torah-level rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'והבשר אשר יגע בכל טמא', once every liquid has been ruled out.

steps.title: Maybe the cow was still wet from a river
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The פסוק could be talking about a שלמים cow that was led through a river and slaughtered while still wet.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps the פסוק is like what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: for example, a person had a cow that was a שלמים offering. He led it through a river and slaughtered it while it was still wet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof of the last step. It shows another way the meat could have become able to receive טומאה without חיבת הקודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every liquid was ruled out. Ordinary river water does do הכשר, and if the animal was slaughtered while still wet, that water made the meat able to become טמא. So the פסוק no longer proves that חיבת הקודש is from the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: And perhaps (bringing up another possibility that weakens a proof)
Peace offerings, whose meat is eaten by the owners
Liquid wet enough to make something else wet

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a classic way a proof by elimination falls apart. If even one possibility was left out, the conclusion does not follow.

phrases.english: But perhaps it is like what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel,
for Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
For example, where a person had a cow
that was a peace offering,
and he led it through the river,
and slaughtered it while wet liquid was still on it.
phrases.notes: That river water is an ordinary liquid, so it gives the meat its הכשר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undermines the elimination proof of step 17 by pointing to a liquid that was not considered.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from 'והבשר אשר יגע בכל טמא' that חיבת הקודש is from the Torah.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The elimination missed river water: a שלמים cow slaughtered while still wet already received הכשר from ordinary liquid.

steps.title: A new proof from the end of the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new proof from the end of the פסוק: the extra word "והבשר" comes to include sacred wood and frankincense.
steps.simpleTranslation: Instead, prove it from the end of the פסוק: "and the flesh" comes to include wood and frankincense.
steps.whatsHappening: The first proof was rejected, so the גמרא switches to the last part of the same פסוק. It reads the extra word "והבשר" as including wood and frankincense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק could be explained by a wet animal, as we saw in step 18. The end of the פסוק repeats "והבשר" for no clear reason, so it is used to add sacred wood and frankincense to the law of טומאה. This sets up the key point in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter part of a text (here, the end of the פסוק)
To include something extra
Wood (for burning on the מזבח)
Frankincense

phrases.english: Rather, prove it from the latter part of the verse:
phrases.notes: Same פסוק as before, ויקרא 7:19. Now we look at its end.

phrases.english: "And the flesh" comes to include wood and frankincense.
phrases.notes: "And the flesh" appears a second time in this פסוק, and that repeat is what gets learned from.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof from the first half of the פסוק, which was rejected in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: That חיבת הקודש can make something able to become טמא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra word "והבשר" at the end of ויקרא 7:19, which includes wood and frankincense.

steps.title: Wood and frankincense are not food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that wood and frankincense are not edible, so normally they could not become טמא the way food does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are wood and frankincense things that are eaten?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that expects the answer "no." This sets up the next move: if they are not food, something else must make them able to become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally only food, after it has been made wet, can become טמא as food. Wood and frankincense are not food at all. So the פסוק including them needs a different explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Things that are eaten; edible

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a real attack on the proof. The question builds the proof by showing that being food cannot be the reason.

phrases.english: Are wood and frankincense edible?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sharpens the proof from step 19 by showing that wood and frankincense are not food.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can non-food items like wood and frankincense become טמא?

steps.title: The holiness itself makes them able to become טמא
steps.stepSummary: The only explanation is that חיבת הקודש makes wood and frankincense able to become טמא and gives them the status of food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the special status of holiness makes them able to become טמא, and makes them count as food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. Holiness is what makes wood and frankincense able to become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wood and frankincense are not food and were never made wet. Their holy status alone puts them in the food category for טומאה. This is the exact idea the גמרא has been trying to prove.

keyTerms.meaning: The special status of holy things
Makes it able to receive טומאה
Food

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that חיבת הקודש can take the place of the usual requirements for טומאה, both being food and being made wet.

phrases.english: Rather, regard for holiness makes them able to become impure,
and makes them count as food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חיבת הקודש makes wood and frankincense able to become טמא and gives them the status of food.

steps.title: The same applies to our case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא applies the rule to the case it is discussing: חיבת הקודש makes it able to become טמא as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, the special status of holiness makes them able to become טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the rule it just proved and applies it to the case under discussion, the dry flour of a מנחה that was never mixed with oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If holiness can make wood and frankincense able to become טמא, it can do the same for dry holy flour. No liquid is needed. This new proof from the end of the פסוק replaces the earlier proof from its beginning, which step 18 rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too; the same applies in this case

steps.whatToRemember: The end of the פסוק includes wood and frankincense, which are not food. So חיבת הקודש alone can make holy items able to become טמא, and this applies to the dry flour of a מנחה too.

phrases.english: Here too, regard for holiness makes them able to become impure.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the dry flour of the מנחה that was never mixed with oil, the case being discussed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from step 21 to the case under discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: חיבת הקודש makes holy items able to become טמא even without liquid, as shown by wood and frankincense.
